entries.name: The Community Association for Riders with Disabilities (CARD)
entries.description: Charity offering therapeutic horseback riding in G. Ross Lord Park in Toronto for children (from age 4) and adults with disabilities, including autism. Classes have at most four riders grouped by age, ability and goals, some with a cognitive focus, and CARD says riding helps sensory processing, focus and communication.
entries.cost_note: $100 intake assessment; $60-65 per lesson, paid for each 9-11 week term.
entries.evidence: CARD's therapeutic horseback riding program benefits riders who seek physical or cognitive therapies, who have a variety of disabilities, including Autism, Down Syndrome, cerebral palsy, and multiple sclerosis.
entries.notes: Fall 2026 session runs September 21 to December 5, 2026. New riders send an application package and have an on-site intake assessment. Instructors are certified through CanTRA, PATH International and/or OEF.

entries.name: Sunrise Therapeutic Riding & Learning Centre
entries.description: Therapeutic riding centre on a farm in Puslinch, between Guelph and Cambridge, for children and adults with special needs, including autism and ADHD. A physiotherapist, occupational therapist and/or speech-language pathologist assesses each new rider and helps set goals, CanTRA-certified instructors teach the lessons, and grooming lessons and integrated summer camps are also offered.
entries.cost_note: Lesson fees plus a yearly membership fee; a scholarship fund helps riders who cannot afford the fees.
entries.evidence: Our Therapeutic Riding program is designed for individuals aged 3 & up with physical and/or cognitive special needs, including (but not limited to) those with autism, ADHD, developmental delays
entries.notes: Admission needs a physician referral form and an assessment visit; the centre reports an ongoing wait list of a few months, and Saturday and weekday-evening spots are limited. Pages are undated but list current programs.

entries.name: SARI Therapeutic Riding
entries.description: Charity in Arva, Ontario, offering adaptive horseback riding for people with disabilities, with each lesson tailored to the rider, including the horse, equipment and teaching style. Its grooming program suits riders who are anxious or need a slow introduction to new activities, and occupational therapy sessions use the horse's movement for sensory and cognitive goals.
entries.cost_note: 2025/26 adaptive riding: $676 (weekdays) or $624 (weekends) for the fall session; $416-468 for winter and spring sessions.
entries.evidence: Also suitable for riders who are anxious/fearful, and need a slow introduction to new activities.
entries.notes: Programs are reserved for participants with a disability; mounted programs need a Physician Referral, and each new participant has an initial OT assessment. The pages do not name autism specifically. Fee schedule is for 2025/26.

entries.name: PRANCE Therapeutic Equestrian Center
entries.description: Therapeutic riding centre near Port Elgin on Lake Huron that has served people with physical, developmental, intellectual and emotional challenges since 1993, for riders aged 5 and up. Ten-week spring and fall sessions are taught by CanTRA-trained instructors, and riders work with the same horse and volunteers as much as possible; day camps and Eagala-model equine therapy for anxiety are also offered.
entries.cost_note: Fees are not published; email or call for an application form.
entries.evidence: Our Therapeutic Equestrian Centre was established in 1993 for the purpose of helping persons with physical, developmental, intellectual and emotional challenges through work with horses.
entries.notes: Same place as the existing ResourceHub listing 'Prance Therapeutic Equestrian Center' (prance.ca). Riders with medical conditions need their physician's approval; contraindications are listed on the sessions page. Street address is from the CanTRA member centre list.

entries.name: Windsor-Essex Therapeutic Riding Association (WETRA)
entries.description: Charity farm near Essex offering therapeutic riding for people with disabilities; most riders are children with developmental, emotional or physical disabilities. An intake assessment sets goals, instructors design each weekly 45-minute lesson for the rider, and un-mounted programs are offered when riding is not suitable.
entries.cost_note: $55 per 45-minute lesson, paid for each 8-12 week session; $80 intake assessment; financial assistance for those who qualify.
entries.evidence: About 80% of those who are enrolled in the program are children who have developmental, emotional or physical disabilities.
entries.notes: Needs a physician referral and an $80 intake assessment; riders under 2 or over 50 are listed as contraindications (exceptions case by case). Fall 2026 and winter 2027 session calendars are posted.

entries.name: Brave-Hearts
entries.description: Small equine learning club on a farm in Lunenburg, Ontario, where children and teens learn reading and math through hands-on horse care, supported by Educational Assistants who are certified equine and learning practitioners. Its quiet farm is aimed at kids with anxiety, ADHD, sensory and learning challenges, with small Saturday groups (Pony Pages, ages 7-11) and private one-to-one sessions on Tuesday afternoons (Stable Mates, ages 6 and up).
entries.cost_note: Pony Pages $360 per 6-week block; Stable Mates private 1:1 $600 per 6-week block.
entries.evidence: Our quiet therapeutic farm environment helps kids who are living with anxiety, ADHD, as well as sensory and learning challenges.
entries.notes: Visits strictly by appointment. Spring, summer and fall session dates are listed without a year (site footer says 2024; it mentions a 2025 award), so confirm current dates. Street address and phone are from the CanTRA member centre list (which spells the town Lunenberg).

entries.name: Therapeutic Riding Association of Ottawa-Carleton (TROtt)
entries.description: Accredited therapeutic riding centre in Greely, Ottawa, for people with physical, mental or developmental disabilities. Its developmental classes build communication and life skills through sensory activities and games, lessons follow each rider's own goals, and unmounted ground programs can be one-on-one.
entries.cost_note: $75 per riding lesson; rider intake assessment $125, or $200 with a physiotherapist.
entries.evidence: Developmental classes: encourages movement exploration and prioritizes the development of communication and life skills through sensory activities and games.
entries.notes: All riders need a doctor's referral and an intake assessment, then may wait for a spot; riding runs in four blocks a year. The existing ResourceHub listing 'Equidae Stables' is also at 6362 Bank Street but has a different name, so it was not linked; a reviewer may want to check.

entries.name: TEAD Therapeutic Riding Centre
entries.description: Farm in Mount Hope, Ontario, offering adaptive riding since 1978 for children, youth and adults with disabilities. CanTRA-certified instructors use adaptive teaching methods and tailor each lesson; the first assessment includes a barn tour, meeting the horses and trying a mechanical horse, and private, semi-private and unmounted grooming lessons are available.
entries.cost_note: Group lesson $75 (60 min), semi-private $100, private $125 (45 min); $45 assessment; $15 yearly membership.
entries.evidence: our CanTRA-certified instructors help individuals with disabilities learn how to ride a horse using adaptive teaching methods and / or specialized equipment. Each lesson is tailored to meet the unique strengths and needs of each participant
entries.notes: Intake form, medical form and assessment are needed before booking lessons; riding lessons are recreation rather than therapy, so usually not billable to insurance. TEAD also lists PD Day programs and clinical services (OT, hippotherapy, psychotherapy). The pages do not name autism specifically.

entries.name: Hope Haven Therapeutic Riding Centre
entries.description: Charity farm near Markdale offering adaptive riding for people of all ages with disabilities or unique needs; its riders include autistic people and people with anxiety. Certified instructors use adaptive teaching techniques, and it also runs a Special Olympics equestrian team, March Break and summer camps for ages 5-13+ that adapt to each camper, and a donor-funded school program for students with disabilities.
entries.cost_note: Adaptive riding: private $60, semi-private $50, group of 3 $45 per lesson; camps $350/week; school program fees sponsored by donors.
entries.evidence: Some common diagnoses of our participants would be Developmental Delay, Down Syndrome, Amputation, Spina Bifida, Cerebral Palsy, Generalized Anxiety and Autism, to name a few.
entries.notes: 2026 camp dates are posted; camps need a Participant Application and Professional Referral Form. The programs page links funding options for Grey County, Town of Blue Mountains and Simcoe County residents, and Passport for adults 18+. Street address is from the CanTRA member centre list.

entries.name: Therapeutic Horsemanship & Riding In Lindsay (T.H.R.I.L.)
entries.description: Charity offering CanTRA-certified therapeutic horsemanship and riding on a farm near Lindsay for children, youth and adults with a diagnosed disability; riders include people with ADHD, social anxiety, learning disabilities and autism. Weekly lessons on trained therapy horses and ponies work on balance, coordination and spatial awareness as well as communication and social skills.
entries.cost_note: Offered at minimal cost to participants, supported by donations and volunteers.
entries.evidence: we have a wide range of challenges in our program - ADHD, social anxiety, learning disabilities, and autism spectrum disorders
entries.notes: Fall 2026 lesson dates (October 2026) are on the site calendar. Riders must have an acquired or congenital diagnosed disability; ages 4 to 90. Located at Field Of Dreams Farm.

entries.name: 1:1 Adapted Swim Lessons (Variety Village)
entries.description: Sport and recreation centre in Scarborough, Toronto, with inclusive programs for people of all abilities, offering one-to-one adapted swim lessons for swimmers with a disability aged 3 and up. Each 30-minute lesson is tailored to the swimmer's needs and goals, and the centre also has a shallow warm pool.
entries.cost_note: Paid registration for each session; the price is not shown on the programs page.
entries.evidence: 1:1 Adapted Swim lessons are for participants with a disability who would benefit from 1:1 instruction. Lessons are 30 minutes in length and are tailored to the individual's needs and swimming goals
entries.notes: Register through Variety Village's online community portal; a fall 2026 program directory is posted. The programs page does not name autism specifically.

entries.name: After School Program (Variety Village)
entries.description: Inclusive after-school program in Scarborough, Toronto, for children and youth of all abilities aged 4-21, Monday to Friday from 3 to 6 p.m. during the school year. Afternoons mix swimming, adapted sports, climbing, arts and STEM with time to relax and socialize, with a 1:5 staff-to-child ratio and optional one-to-one reading support.
entries.cost_note: $37 per day or $170 per week; optional snack ($5/day), 1:1 reading ($10/day) and bus pick-up ($5/day).
entries.evidence: Supervised by qualified staff, the program emphasizes social interaction and safe participation with a 1:5 staff-to-child ratio.
entries.notes: Registration is for a full session (fall, winter or spring); 2026-2027 school year registration is open. Walking pick-up from Birchcliff Heights PS and bus pick-up from Birch Cliff PS. The pages do not name autism specifically.

entries.name: Adapted Swim for Life and Sensory Friendly Swims (City of Mississauga)
entries.description: City of Mississauga swim programs: Adapted Swim for Life lessons for swimmers with disabilities at a 1:3 instructor ratio, where swimmers work at their own pace and staff may call ahead about triggers and sensory needs. Sensory Friendly Swims for all ages offer a calm pool with no music, minimal whistles and quiet changerooms, and the Snoezelen Pool Program uses dimmed lights and soft water sprays; no diagnosis is required.
entries.cost_note: Regular lesson and drop-in swim fees; costs are on the city's program pages.
entries.evidence: Sensory Friendly Swim is a relaxing, unstructured swim for all ages, designed to support individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder, Sensory Processing Disorder, or medical needs.
entries.notes: Snoezelen and sensory swims need a caregiver (14+) in the water where appropriate. Days and pools are on the city's swim schedules. The city also runs adapted skating, arts and Children in Motion programs.

entries.name: Adapted Aquatics (City of Richmond Hill)
entries.description: City of Richmond Hill swim program for children and adults with disabilities at Bayview Hill Pool, Oak Ridges Pool and The Wave Pool. Children learn to swim at their own pace without a set curriculum, taught by volunteers supervised by a specialized instructor, and private one-to-one lessons are recommended for swimmers with special needs who are not comfortable in a group.
entries.cost_note: Program fees apply; an inclusion membership is required.
entries.evidence: Children will learn to swim at their own pace without the restrictions of a structured curriculum. Adapted Aquatics is conducted by volunteers under the supervision of a specialized instructor.
entries.notes: Contact Inclusion Services before registering to discuss individual needs and the support offered. Private lessons are offered when available.

entries.name: Adapted Aquatics (City of Toronto Parks and Recreation)
entries.description: City of Toronto swim activities for people with a disability or special needs: Adapted Ultra Swim (one instructor to three swimmers, at each swimmer's own level), a free Adapted Leisure Swim drop-in for families, adapted aquatic games, and the Adapted SPLASH swim team. Adapted activities use smaller groups and need an Adapted and Inclusive Services membership.
entries.cost_note: Adapted Leisure Swim drop-in is free; fees for registered swim activities are not listed on this page.
entries.evidence: A progressive activity that encourages swimmers with a disability or special needs to expand their comfort in the water, develop their swimming skills and participate at a level appropriate for their ability.
entries.notes: New users call the Adapted and Inclusive Services hotline at least four weeks before registration to be assessed for a membership. People who need 1:1 personal, behavioural or medical support bring their own support person (14+); caregivers may need to give 1:1 support in the water.

entries.name: Sensory-Friendly Swim (City of Guelph)
entries.description: Drop-in swim in the leisure pool at Guelph's West End Community Centre for children, youth and adults with autism, sensory processing differences or learning disabilities. The swim is set up to reduce stimuli and create a sensory-friendly environment.
entries.cost_note: Drop-in swim; the admission fee is not stated on this page.
entries.evidence: The Sensory Friendly Swim is for adults, youth and children living with Autism Spectrum Disorder, sensory processing and/or learning disabilities. This swim is designed to reduce stimuli and create a sensory friendly environment
entries.notes: Pre-register for drop-in swims online, in person or by phone (519-837-5699) up to 23 hours before. Days and times are in the fall/winter 2026 drop-in schedule linked from the page.

entries.name: Adapted Aquatics and Inclusive Swim Lessons (City of Kitchener)
entries.description: City of Kitchener swim lessons for children and youth with special needs. Adapted Aquatics Beginner (age 4+) is one-to-one with a volunteer in the warm-water pool, with transition time built into each 40-minute class; Inclusive Swim Lessons have a swim instructor and an inclusion support worker for every three swimmers, and Adapted Fit Swim (13+) suits confident swimmers.
entries.cost_note: Program fees apply; an Inclusion Membership is required to register.
entries.evidence: Adapted Aquatics—Beginner is for children and youth with special needs and little or no swim experience. The program will take place in our warm-water pool. The ratio is 1-1 with a volunteer.
entries.notes: 2026-2027 registration dates are listed on the page. Inclusive Swim Lessons currently cover Kitchener Swims Child 1 and Child 2; call Inclusion Services (519-904-5793) about support in other levels.

entries.name: Adapted Swim Lessons (City of Burlington)
entries.description: City of Burlington adaptive aquatic program for children with physical, developmental or sensory needs. A parent or caregiver is in the water with the child, who gets personal attention while building water confidence and basic swimming skills.
entries.cost_note: Fees are not listed on the swim lessons page.
entries.evidence: Our Adaptive Aquatic Program is designed to support children with diverse physical, developmental, or sensory needs in a safe, inclusive, and engaging water environment.
entries.notes: Phone is the City of Burlington's main line. Age range and schedule are not given on the page; check the city's registration system.

entries.name: Adapted Aquatics for Teens and Adults (City of Waterloo)
entries.description: City of Waterloo swim program for people 12 and older with physical, developmental or behavioural special needs who have little or no swimming experience. One instructor works with up to two swimmers, with extra volunteer support.
entries.cost_note: Fees are not listed on this page; the city lists financial and inclusion support.
entries.evidence: This program is available for individuals 12 years or older with special needs (physical, developmental, behavioural) who have little or no swimming experience and require specialized instruction.
entries.notes: The city also lends sensory backpacks and offers inclusion support (linked from the same page).

entries.name: Adapted Swim (Town of Ajax)
entries.description: Town of Ajax Swim for Life lessons for swimmers aged 3 to 17 with differing abilities, where each skill is broken into small, manageable steps so swimmers learn at their own pace through repetition. Private 1:1 lessons (ages 3-18) focus on individual needs outside a group.
entries.cost_note: Fees are not listed on the swimming lessons page.
entries.evidence: Each skill is broken down into small manageable steps to create a positive learning environment and make the success of each swimmer more achievable.
entries.notes: Phone is the Ajax Community Centre (75 Centennial Rd.); lessons also run at McLean Community Centre and Audley Recreation Centre.

entries.name: Adapted Swim and Low Sensory Public Swim (Municipality of Clarington)
entries.description: Municipality of Clarington recreational swims for people with physical or developmental disabilities and a caregiver at the Diane Hamre Recreation Complex from September to June, with caregivers and support workers admitted free. Clarington also runs Low Sensory Public Swims for all ages, with water features off and noise kept to a minimum.
entries.cost_note: Regular swim admission; caregivers and support workers enter free.
entries.evidence: A sensory-friendly swimming experience for all ages. During this swim, water features will remain off and noise will be kept to a minimum.
entries.notes: Times are on the facility swim schedules; call the facility at 905-623-3379.

entries.name: For Reasons Of Disability Private Swim Lessons (City of Sault Ste. Marie)
entries.description: Private one-to-one swimming lessons at the John Rhodes Community Centre pool for people who benefit from extra support and individual attention, including people with developmental or cognitive support needs. Families request a lesson through an online form.
entries.cost_note: Private lesson fees are listed in the city's swim lesson price table.
entries.evidence: For Reasons Of Disability Private Swim Lessons (FROD) is designed for individuals who benefit from the additional support and individualized attention provided through private swimming lessons, including those with physical, developmental, cognitive, or other support needs.
entries.notes: Fall 2026 lesson registration began September 22, 2026. The city's pool admission policy asks that swimmers with a disability come with a 1:1 support person who knows their needs. The city has a Municipal Autism Strategy (linked from its accessibility pages).

entries.name: Fiddlehead Care Farm
entries.description: Care farm on 50 acres in Mono, Dufferin County, offering animal-assisted counselling, life-skills and group programs for children, teens and young adults with unique needs, including autism, ADHD and developmental disabilities. Sessions with a social worker and a certified child life specialist happen in a quiet, natural setting with farm animals, and the Co-Care Farmers program teaches animal care and farm skills to youth with developmental, sensory or mental health needs. No referral or diagnosis is needed.
entries.cost_note: Fees are not listed on the pages checked; contact the farm.
entries.evidence: We help people who are coping with anxiety and depression, social difficulties, emotional problems, grief, trauma and negative self-esteem. We support those with autism, ADHD and developmental disabilities.
entries.notes: Listed as an established care farm in the Care Farming Network directory. Little Care Farmers (infants to preschoolers with caregivers) ran Tuesday mornings in 2026, with a fall session September 8 to October 27, 2026. The phone number is listed for a named staff member (Stephanie).

entries.name: Autism Service Dogs (Canadian Guide Dogs for the Blind)
entries.description: Ottawa-area charity, known for guide dogs, that now trains and places autism service dogs with autistic children in the greater Ottawa area, for children aged 2 to 5 at the time of application. The dogs give companionship, grounding and confidence to children who may struggle with overstimulation, communication or anxiety in public, and families do 2-4 weeks of intensive training once matched.
entries.cost_note: Free to accepted applicants (a nominal $1 lease fee); families pay for the dog's food and vet care.
entries.evidence: The dogs are trained to provide companionship, grounding and confidence for children who may struggle with overstimulation, communication or anxiety in public settings.
entries.notes: Pilot program reported in local news in January 2026; the program page says the waitlist is open, with random selection if submissions exceed spots. Families read the information package, then send the Expression of Interest form to info@guidedogs.ca.

entries.name: Paws 4 Stories (St. John Ambulance Therapy Dog Program, Barrie Simcoe Muskoka)
entries.description: Volunteer therapy dog teams from St. John Ambulance's Barrie Simcoe Muskoka branch serve Simcoe and York counties. In the Paws 4 Stories reading program, children read aloud to a calm, non-judgemental dog without being interrupted, a low-pressure way to build reading confidence and skills.
entries.cost_note: The listing says fees: none.
entries.evidence: Paws 4 Stories program helps children build confidence as they learn to read with the non-judgemental presence of a dog, allowing children to read without interruption, improving reading skills and self-esteem
entries.notes: From the Simcoe County community services database (last full update January 20, 2026). Sessions depend on library partners and volunteer availability, so ask the local library or the branch. St. John Ambulance's own therapy dog page (sja.ca) blocked automated checking.

entries.name: Reading with the Dogs (Hanover Public Library)
entries.description: After-school reading sessions in the children's area of the Hanover Public Library, where children practise reading aloud to St. John Ambulance certified therapy dogs and their volunteers, with a library book or a favourite from home. The library says reading to a dog helps children relax and stop feeling nervous about reading, which suits children who find reading aloud stressful.
entries.cost_note: Library program; cost not stated. Spaces can fill up.
entries.evidence: When a child reads with a certified therapy dog, they begin to relax and forget about feeling nervous about reading.
entries.notes: The program description is from an earlier March session page; the library's events list shows Reading with the Dogs on October 21, 22 and 29 and November 5, 2026, 4-5 p.m. Same place as the existing ResourceHub listing 'Hanover Public Library'.

entries.name: S.W.A.M. Toronto (S.W.A.M. Canada)
entries.description: University of Toronto student chapter of S.W.A.M. Canada (formerly Making Waves) giving low-cost one-to-one swimming lessons to children and youth with disabilities, including autism, ADHD and sensory differences. Each child has a 30-minute weekly lesson with the same volunteer instructor all session, with no set curriculum, at the Beverly School Pool.
entries.cost_note: Low cost; the price is set by each chapter.
entries.evidence: Lessons are one-on-one, for 30 minutes, once a week with the same instructor for the duration of the session. There is no specific curriculum so instructors will work with the swimmers on their specific needs and goals.
entries.notes: Registration is first come, first served and demand often exceeds capacity; a winter registration link was posted in October 2026. The chapter can remove a swimmer who repeatedly endangers themselves or others at the pool.

entries.name: S.W.A.M. Hamilton (S.W.A.M. Canada)
entries.description: McMaster University student chapter of S.W.A.M. Canada giving low-cost one-to-one swimming lessons to children and youth with disabilities, including autism, ADHD and sensory differences. Each child has a 30-minute weekly lesson with the same volunteer instructor all session, with no set curriculum, at the Boys and Girls Club Hamilton-Halton pool.
entries.cost_note: Low cost; the price is set by each chapter.
entries.evidence: Lessons are one-on-one, for 30 minutes, once a week with the same instructor for the duration of the session. There is no specific curriculum so instructors will work with the swimmers on their specific needs and goals.
entries.notes: The fall 2026 session is full; the chapter posts future registration dates on its social media. Free parking beside the pool.

entries.name: S.W.A.M. Kingston (S.W.A.M. Canada)
entries.description: Queen's University student chapter of S.W.A.M. Canada giving low-cost one-to-one swimming lessons to children and youth with disabilities, including autism, ADHD and sensory differences. Each child has a 30-minute weekly lesson with the same volunteer instructor all session, with no set curriculum, at the Queen's Athletics & Recreation Centre pool.
entries.cost_note: Low cost; the price is set by each chapter.
entries.evidence: Lessons are one-on-one, for 30 minutes, once a week with the same instructor for the duration of the session. There is no specific curriculum so instructors will work with the swimmers on their specific needs and goals.
entries.notes: Registration is first come, first served through a link on the chapter page; demand often exceeds capacity.

entries.name: S.W.A.M. London (S.W.A.M. Canada)
entries.description: Western University student chapter of S.W.A.M. Canada giving low-cost one-to-one swimming lessons to children and youth with disabilities, including autism, ADHD and sensory differences. Each child has a 30-minute weekly lesson with the same volunteer instructor all session, with no set curriculum, at the Finan Swim School pool on Sugarcreek Trail.
entries.cost_note: Low cost; the price is set by each chapter.
entries.evidence: Lessons are one-on-one, for 30 minutes, once a week with the same instructor for the duration of the session. There is no specific curriculum so instructors will work with the swimmers on their specific needs and goals.
entries.notes: A fall registration link is posted on the chapter page; demand often exceeds capacity. Free parking nearby.

entries.name: S.W.A.M. Sudbury (S.W.A.M. Canada)
entries.description: Sudbury chapter of S.W.A.M. Canada giving low-cost one-to-one swimming lessons to children and youth with disabilities, including autism, ADHD and sensory differences. Each child has a 30-minute lesson with the same volunteer instructor all session on Sunday mornings at the YMCA of Northeastern Ontario pool, with no set curriculum.
entries.cost_note: Low cost; the price is set by each chapter.
entries.evidence: Lessons are one-on-one and 30 minutes long, with swimmers working with the same instructor throughout the session. Lessons take place on Sundays between 9:00 and 10:30 a.m.
entries.notes: Two sessions a year: fall (September to November) and winter (January to March). Fall 2026 registration is closed; watch the chapter's social media for winter dates.

entries.name: West End After School Respite Program (Community Living Toronto)
entries.description: After-school program in Toronto's west end for youth aged 11-17 with autism, from 3 to 6 p.m. during the fall 2026 session. Activities include homework help, crafts, puzzles, board games, movies, a trampoline, iPad games, outdoor play and a sensory room.
entries.cost_note: $10 per day.
entries.evidence: Activities include: Help with homework, colouring, themed crafts, puzzles, board games, movies, trampoline, iPad games, sensory room, and outdoor activities.
entries.notes: Posted on ConnectABILITY (Community Living Toronto) in May 2026 for the session running September 8 to December 18, 2026. Apply by phone or through the email of the named staff contact on the page.

entries.name: Galloway After School Program (GASP) (Strides Toronto)
entries.description: After-school social, life-skills and activity group in Scarborough for youth aged 12-18 diagnosed with autism or a mild to moderate developmental disability. In a structured setting, participants practise cooking, street safety, hygiene, understanding emotions and healthy relationships, with outings; it runs Monday and Tuesday 3-6 p.m. and Wednesday and Thursday 3-7:15 p.m.
entries.cost_note: Costs are discussed at the intake appointment.
entries.evidence: GASP helps meet individual needs and provides a safe, structured, and fun environment where they can learn and develop more independence skills.
entries.notes: Hours are from the Toronto Central Healthline listing (last updated May 4, 2026), which gives 416-724-7444 for intake; the Strides page gives 416-438-3697 (option 1). Strides also runs a Galloway Saturday Respite program for ages 12-35.

entries.name: ASD After School Social Skills Programs (Simcoe County District School Board)
entries.description: Seasonal after-school programs for Simcoe County District School Board students with a developmental profile consistent with autism, in person and online: a coding and robotics club, music and recreation social skills groups, a teamwork-based problem-solving program and the Secret Agent Society program for ages 8-12. Parents may join some sessions and get resources to practise skills at home, and SIBSHOPs workshops serve siblings.
entries.cost_note: Cost is not stated on the program posts.
entries.evidence: In April and May, the Simcoe County District School Board (SCDSB) is offering a variety of inclusive, after-school social and recreational programs for students with a developmental profile consistent with autism spectrum disorder (ASD)
entries.notes: For SCDSB students only. Runs in seasonal blocks (winter January-March and spring April-May 2026 were posted, with earlier rounds in 2024 and 2025); apply at scdsb.on.ca/inclusiverecreationprograms. Applicants may be screened, and places are limited. Check for a fall or winter 2026-27 round.

entries.name: Autism Assistance Dog Guides (Lions Foundation of Canada Dog Guides)
entries.description: Lions Foundation of Canada Dog Guides trains and places Autism Assistance Dog Guides with autistic children aged 3 to 12 across Canada, for safety and companionship. Families train on campus at the Oakville facility, an instructor visits at home within 4-8 weeks, and support continues until the dog retires; dogs are provided at no cost.
entries.cost_note: Dog Guides are provided at no cost to qualified applicants.
entries.evidence: Autism Assistance Dog Guides assist children (ages 3-12) on the autism spectrum. These Dog Guides provide safety, companionship and unconditional love.
entries.notes: As of October 2026 applications are closed to new families, with no reopening date posted; previous clients can re-apply for a successor dog by email. The organization receives no government funding.

entries.name: Service Dog for Youth with ASD (Mira)
entries.description: Quebec-based organization that has provided service dogs since 2010 to autistic young people aged 5 to 21 who live in Canada, selected and trained to calm, protect and support the child. The child and a parent attend a 9-day training class at Mira with free accommodation and meals, and the dog itself is free.
entries.cost_note: Dog provided free of charge; families must cover the dog's care (about $3,500 a year).
entries.evidence: Since 2010, Mira has been providing service dogs to young people with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). These dogs, specially selected and trained, help to calm, protect, and support the children
entries.notes: Applications open in waves; as of October 2026 the application link is closed. Applicants must live in Canada and send a recent ASD diagnostic report; a clinical team and committee review each case.

entries.name: Paws to Read and Paws-Abilities (Therapeutic Paws of Canada)
entries.description: Charity whose volunteer therapy dog and cat teams visit schools, libraries and facilities. In Paws to Read, children who find reading out loud hard read to a calm, non-judgmental pet, and Paws-Abilities visits are tailored with occupational therapists and other professionals to goals such as social interaction, attentiveness and calming.
entries.cost_note: Paws to Read is free for primary schools and libraries.
entries.evidence: Children can struggle with reading at different stages of their learning and may have difficulty or be uncomfortable reading out loud or in front of a group.
entries.notes: Visits are arranged through local Team Leaders, usually via a school, library or facility rather than by families directly. The page footer is dated 2023, so check which areas currently have teams. Mailing address is a PO Box in Hampton, Ontario.

entries.name: S.W.A.M. Canada (formerly Making Waves)
entries.description: Student-run not-for-profit with chapters in Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick giving low-cost one-to-one swimming lessons to children and youth (usually 3-18) with disabilities, including autism, ADHD and sensory differences. Each swimmer has a 30-minute weekly lesson with the same trained volunteer all session, with a flexible plan built around the child's needs.
entries.cost_note: Low cost; the price is set by each chapter.
entries.evidence: Each swimmer receives a 30 minute weekly lesson with the same instructor throughout the session. Lessons are designed to meet each child where they're at
entries.notes: Chapters listed: Hamilton, Halifax, Kingston, London, Montréal, Ottawa, Saint John, Sudbury and Toronto (chapters with their own pages are listed separately). Formerly known as MakingWaves and SwimAbility; began in Montréal in 2009. Volunteers are supervised by lesson coordinators and lifeguards.

entries.name: MOVE by GoodLife Kids (GoodLife Kids Foundation)
entries.description: Free fitness program for youth aged 12-21 with autism or intellectual disabilities, with small virtual classes open anywhere in Canada and in-person classes at select GoodLife Fitness clubs, usually 2-3 times a week in the evenings or on weekends. Coaches are certified fitness professionals trained to work with autistic participants, and each new participant has a meet-and-greet with their coach before the first class.
entries.cost_note: Free; funded by donors and fundraising such as the MOVE 4 Kids event.
entries.evidence: Prior to attending your first class your MOVE Coach will set up a 'meet and greet' meeting with the participant and any caregivers that would like to attend.
entries.notes: Caregivers must stay for in-person classes; free Try-it classes run on the third Tuesday of each month. The site says 15 new in-person locations were added. Head office is in London, Ontario (Toronto Central Healthline listing, updated June 15, 2026).

entries.name: Autism Service Dogs (BC & Alberta Guide Dogs)
entries.description: Charity that trains certified Autism Service Dogs for children with moderate to profound autism aged 3 to 7 (at application) in British Columbia and Alberta, provided free to families. The dogs aim to make the child safer and to reduce stress in school, social and leisure settings; applying involves interviews and an in-home visit by a certified instructor.
entries.cost_note: Dogs are free to families; families pay for the dog's ongoing care.
entries.evidence: An Autism Service Dog can improve the child's ability to participate in education, social and leisure activities because the canine may reduce the stress associated with these situations.
entries.notes: As of October 2026 applications for all areas are closed because of a multi-year waitlist. Also serves Alberta (403-258-0819). Autism must be the child's primary disability, with a confirmed diagnosis.

entries.name: Story PALS (Pet Access League Society)
entries.description: Calgary non-profit whose volunteer therapy dog teams run Story PALS with Calgary Public Library: struggling readers aged 6-12 are paired one-on-one with a therapy dog for a 6-week session. Children read without fear of being criticized or interrupted, which helps those who find reading in front of others hard.
entries.cost_note: Not stated; sessions are run with Calgary Public Library.
entries.evidence: For a 6-week session, struggling readers, aged 6-12 years old, are paired up with PALS therapy dog teams for one-on-one reading sessions.
entries.notes: Run with Calgary Public Library since 2006; check the library's program listings for current sessions. PALS also visits schools, the Alberta Children's Hospital and other facilities.

entries.name: Paws to Read (Halifax Public Libraries)
entries.description: Reading sessions at several Halifax public library branches where children in grades 1-5 are matched one-on-one with a certified therapy dog and its volunteer handler for 30-minute bookings, several of them right after school. Reading aloud to a calm, attentive dog is a low-pressure way for children to build confidence in reading.
entries.cost_note: Library program; sign up in advance (cost not stated).
entries.evidence: Your child will be matched with a reading therapy dog and their volunteer handler
entries.notes: Fall 2026 sessions include Halifax Central Library (Mondays 6-7 p.m., October 19 to November 16, full), Tantallon (Fridays 3:45-5:45 p.m., October 16 to November 20, open) and Woodlawn (Tuesdays 3:30-4:30 p.m., October 13 to November 10, full); spots fill quickly. Dogs and handlers are certified by Therapeutic Paws of Canada (national entry). Runs at several branches, so it is not linked to the existing Halifax Central Library listing.

entries.name: Swim, Skate and Multisport Programs (Canucks Autism Network)
entries.description: BC charity running sports, recreation and social programs for autistic children, youth and adults; children's core programs are Multisport, Swim and Skate, building movement and social skills. Programs use highly trained staff and a high ratio of staff and volunteers so each participant is supported at their level, in Metro Vancouver, the Fraser Valley, Kamloops, Kelowna, Nanaimo and Victoria, with virtual programs province-wide.
entries.cost_note: Free CAN account; most programs have a highly subsidized fee, reimbursable through Autism Funding or CAN's Fee Assistance Program.
entries.evidence: A high ratio of staff and volunteers to ensure that each participant is supported at their level and encouraging independence, whenever possible.
entries.notes: Participants must live in BC; proof of diagnosis is needed for ages 0-12, while ages 13+ can self-identify. Fall 2026 registration opened August 30, 2026 and the fall season runs September to December. Other children's programs (gymnastics, hockey, music) vary by location.

entries.name: Creston Valley Society for Therapeutic Horsemanship
entries.description: CanTRA-accredited therapeutic riding centre in Creston offering mounted and unmounted equine-assisted activities for people of all ages, set up for riders with autism, ADHD, sensory processing disorder or learning disabilities as well as physical and mental health conditions. Lessons run in an 8-week spring session, two 4-week summer sessions and an 8-week fall session.
entries.cost_note: Fees are in the rider application package, not on the home page.
entries.evidence: To promote health by providing mounted and unmounted therapeutic equine-assisted activities to individuals diagnosed with physical and mental health conditions such as autism, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, sensory processing disorder, or learning disabilities.
entries.notes: 2026 sessions: spring March 30 to May 25, summer June 15 to August 7, fall September 7 to October 30, 2026. New riders complete an application package.

entries.name: North Fraser Therapeutic Riding Association
entries.description: Charity in Maple Ridge offering therapeutic riding for children and adults with physical, mental, developmental, emotional or social challenges, with CanTRA-certified instructors planning each rider's program after an assessment. Riders choose private or semi-private sessions, and parents describe gains in regulation, language and social skills; there is also a summer camp for children.
entries.cost_note: Fees are not listed on the home page.
entries.evidence: Our riders experience physical, mental, developmental, emotional or social challenges and each therapeutic program is designed to meet their needs. Our riders can choose either private or semi-private sessions.
entries.notes: The site's phone (604 462 7786) differs from the CanTRA list (604-462-7768); the site's number is used. Mailing address is in Pitt Meadows.

entries.name: Southlands Therapeutic Riding Society (STaRS)
entries.description: Charity in Vancouver's Southlands offering CanTRA-certified therapeutic riding for children and adults with physical, developmental, cognitive and/or mental health disabilities. Lessons take place at stables and an urban heritage farm with goats, chickens and a duck pond, in a setting the society describes as soothing and serene, and it also offers equine-assisted learning.
entries.cost_note: Fees are not listed on the pages checked.
entries.evidence: STaRS operates primarily at Shannon Stables, Thistle Stables, and Southlands Heritage Farm, an urban farm consisting of a 17-stall horse barn, a heritage orchard, market garden, duck pond, goats, and chickens. The atmosphere is soothing and serene
entries.notes: Program details and fees were not on the pages checked; contact the society. Instructors gained CHA certification through a STaRS-hosted program (posted on the home page).

entries.name: Pacific Riding for Developing Abilities (PRDA)
entries.description: Charity in Langley, beside Campbell Valley Regional Park, offering individualized adaptive riding year-round for riders with diverse cognitive and/or physical abilities from age 3. Adaptive equipment and settings are matched to each rider, from riding independently with an instructor to support from up to five trained people.
entries.cost_note: 2026 schedule and fees are posted on the registration page (PDF).
entries.evidence: We specialize in serving individuals with a wide range of diverse cognitive and/or physical abilities, starting as young as 3 years of age.
entries.notes: Summer 2026 ran as two mini sessions (July 6-31 and August 4-28). Also offers short-term rehabilitation riding after an assessment. The pages do not name autism specifically.

entries.name: Rainbow Riders Therapeutic Riding Centre
entries.description: Therapeutic riding centre in Pippy Park, St. John's, for children and adults of all ages with physical, emotional, cognitive or social disabilities, including autism and ADHD. Lessons are taught by CanTRA-certified instructors, and a developmental paediatrician quoted on its page notes that even caring for the horses can lower anxiety and help self-regulation.
entries.cost_note: Fees are not listed on the therapeutic riding page.
entries.evidence: I have seen kids who participate only in the care of the horses also have tremendous benefits with decreased anxiety and improved self-regulation.
entries.notes: Each rider needs a physician referral form and a registration form. Footer is dated 2022 but the programs page says it is reaching more participants than ever.

entries.name: S.W.A.M. Halifax (S.W.A.M. Canada)
entries.description: Dalhousie University student chapter of S.W.A.M. Canada giving low-cost one-to-one swimming lessons to children and youth with disabilities, including autism, ADHD and sensory differences. Each child has a 30-minute weekly lesson with the same volunteer instructor all session, with no set curriculum, at the Halifax Centennial Pool.
entries.cost_note: Low cost; the price is set by each chapter.
entries.evidence: Lessons are one-on-one, for 30 minutes, once a week with the same instructor for the duration of the session. There is no specific curriculum so instructors will work with the swimmers on their specific needs and goals.
entries.notes: The registration link was marked 'coming soon' in October 2026; email the chapter for the next session.

entries.name: S.W.A.M. Saint John (S.W.A.M. Canada)
entries.description: University of New Brunswick (Saint John) student chapter of S.W.A.M. Canada giving low-cost one-to-one swimming lessons to children and youth with disabilities, including autism, ADHD and sensory differences. Each child has a 30-minute weekly lesson with the same volunteer instructor all session, with no set curriculum, at the Simonds High School pool.
entries.cost_note: Low cost; the price is set by each chapter.
entries.evidence: Lessons are one-on-one, for 30 minutes, once a week with the same instructor for the duration of the session. There is no specific curriculum so instructors will work with the swimmers on their specific needs and goals.
entries.notes: Registration updates are posted on the chapter's social media; it was recruiting fall 2026 volunteers. Free parking at the school.

entries.name: Comox Valley Therapeutic Riding Society (CVTRS)
entries.description: Therapeutic riding centre in Courtenay with Barn Buddies, a class for autistic children aged 5-7 that pairs horse care with a shorter ride to suit attention spans and builds self-regulation skills. It also runs The Stable Program for youth 8-18 with anxiety, trauma or ADHD, and adaptive riding for all ages; classes run Monday to Thursday, September to June.
entries.cost_note: $65 per 40-minute class; works with funders such as Jumpstart, KidSport and Autism Funding.
entries.evidence: The Barn Buddies program is a class designed for our youngest riders who are on the autism spectrum. Due to the riders ages, 5-7 years, they are unable to ride consistently for an hour
entries.notes: Every rider is assessed first and may join a waitlist through the Rider Intake Form; classes run 10am-5pm Monday to Thursday, for 12-30 weeks depending on the program. A 2026-2027 riding calendar is posted.

entries.name: SaltSpring Therapeutic Riding Association (SSTRA)
entries.description: Therapeutic riding and non-riding equine programs on Salt Spring Island for children, youth and adults, including people with anxiety, learning differences or developmental challenges. Lessons are private or in groups of at most two riders, in a calm, structured setting focused on consistency and individual goals, and ground-based sessions suit people who prefer not to ride.
entries.cost_note: Fees are not listed on the programs page.
entries.evidence: Private or small group lessons (max two riders) Calm, structured, supportive environment
entries.notes: Participants need a medical note or referral depending on needs. Fall and spring sessions run 11 weeks, winter 10 weeks. Street address and phone are from the CanTRA member centre list.

entries.name: Free Spirit Therapeutic Riding Association (FSTRA)
entries.description: Therapeutic riding at Rohan Wood Stables in Aylesford, Nova Scotia, for people aged 3 and up who need extra support, including autistic riders and riders with anxiety such as selective mutism or social phobias. Spring and fall sessions guarantee 10 lessons over 12 weeks, with an intake meeting before the first lesson, and there is a summer day camp.
entries.cost_note: $400 per 10-lesson session; summer camp $250.
entries.evidence: You are eligible to participate in our program if you present with any one or more of the following concerns or presentations: ASD (Autism Spectrum Disorder) Anxiety (select mutism, social phobias, panic disorders)
entries.notes: Spring sessions run April to June on Wednesdays and Thursdays; fall runs September to December. Registration forms come from info@fstra.org.

entries.name: Equilibrium Therapeutic Riding
entries.description: Therapeutic riding centre in Osler, Saskatchewan, offering private and group lessons for children and adults with disabilities, including developmental riding therapy for people with differences in cognition, behaviour, language and sensory integration. An introductory assessment uses the child's existing therapy and school plans to tailor the riding program, and weekday lessons run into the early evening from September to June.
entries.cost_note: 2026-27 private lessons $82.42 (30 min) to $131.25 (60 min) including GST; $82.42 introductory assessment.
entries.evidence: Please bring any paperwork related to your/your child's existing programming (PT, OT, SLP reports or classroom or behaviour program plans) with you to the appointment so that we can create a therapeutic riding program tailored to the individual.
entries.notes: Riders with a disability need a physician referral form. Fall/winter 2026-27 private lessons run weekly from September 14, 2026 to June 2027. The phone is from the CanTRA list; the site gives only a local number and a staff member's personal email, so email is left blank.

entries.name: Hinchinbrook Farm
entries.description: Therapeutic riding and recreation farm in Blockhouse, Nova Scotia, whose main clients are families with autism. Lessons are by appointment after an assessment, trained volunteers work one-on-one with each child, equipment and activities are chosen for the individual rider, and the instructor offers the Horse Boy method; there are also summer horsemanship afternoons for ages 9-13.
entries.cost_note: Barn Rats horsemanship sessions $60 per session; riding lesson fees not listed.
entries.evidence: Our prime objective is to provide a therapeutic horse back riding program to support the physical mental and emotional well-being of persons with disabilities. Its main clients are families with autism.
entries.notes: Not a CanTRA centre: the instructor was CanTRA-certified but left in 2012 to offer the Horse Boy program. Riding needs a doctor's referral, waiver and rider insurance; all visits by appointment only. Summer 2026 Barn Rats ran Wednesday afternoons in July and August.

entries.name: Sensory Friendly Swims (City of Surrey)
entries.description: Monthly drop-in swims at Surrey's public pools for autistic people, people with anxiety or sensory processing needs, and their families. Water features and noise are turned down, with no background music or announcements, clear times and transition warnings, sensory break rooms and extra staff, and kits with noise-cancelling headphones, fidgets and communication cards to borrow.
entries.cost_note: Use a Recreation Surrey pass or pay drop-in admission.
entries.evidence: Sensory friendly swims are inclusive swim times for individuals and families looking for an environment with reduced noise. They are available for those who are autistic, have anxiety or other sensory processing needs
entries.notes: Fall 2026 dates: Newton Recreation Centre (October 28, November 25, December 22), South Surrey Indoor Pool (November 7, December 5), Surrey Sport & Leisure Complex (November 9, December 14) and Guildford Recreation Centre (November 18, December 16).

entries.name: Adaptive Swimming Lessons for Kids and Teens (City of Calgary with Vecova)
entries.description: City of Calgary swim lessons for children and teens with disabilities, run with Vecova, with one teacher for every four swimmers and a parent or support person in the water. Lessons adapt to each child's sensory, physical, cognitive and emotional needs, families fill in a needs form beforehand, and swimmers are encouraged to bring familiar comfort items to ease anxiety.
entries.cost_note: City registered program; fees are shown when booking a course.
entries.evidence: adapting lessons to each participant considering sensory, physical, cognitive and emotional needs
entries.notes: Fall 2026 adaptive programs registration was ongoing; register online or call 403-268-3800 (option 1). No prerequisite.

entries.name: Adapted Swim Lessons (City of Regina)
entries.description: City of Regina one-to-one adapted swim lessons for people who experience disability, with instructors working toward each swimmer's own needs and goals, plus adapted group lessons and an Adapted Leisure Swim for people with disabilities and their families. The city also runs free inclusive dance classes for children and youth with disabilities.
entries.cost_note: Fees are not listed on the inclusive programs page.
entries.evidence: This 1-on-1 adapted swim lesson is designed for those that experience disability. Instructors will work with participants to support them in meeting their needs and goals.
entries.notes: City staff facilitate but cannot lift or reposition swimmers. Adapted Leisure Swim runs at the Sandra Schmirler and North West leisure centres; book through Regina Recreation Online or the Playline (306-777-7529).
